correctness.rationale: The connected active-constraint graph criterion is proved by incidence rank. Cross-cluster tightness forces the potential global minimum and maximum to be exactly one apart. Every cluster must possess one of these anchors but not both, and every nonanchor point must be at its cluster internal distance from that anchor or it would be isolated. Conversely the binary anchor core and the internal edges connect every enumerated potential. The product counts disjoint unique potential states for all integer cluster sizes and all independent real \(0<t_i<1\). A complete quarter-grid enumeration independently confirmed 10 heterogeneous rational test profiles; the proof is not extrapolated from the finite tests.

originality.rationale: Material reading found the specific disjoint-pair theorem is a covered special case, not the arbitrary-sized cluster statement; other nearby published facet laws treat intra-cluster distances longer than cross-cluster distances. Gordon–Petrov and Montrucchio–Pistone provide the standard extremality machinery but not the product enumeration. The full connected-tight-graph proof classifies natural block ultrametrics of arbitrary cluster size and independent strict inner scales. Targeted public mathematical-record searches plus primary HTML text inspections revealed no known covering claim; unindexed equivalent formulas remain a bibliographic risk.
residual_risks: Earlier less readily indexed ultrametric Lipschitz-polytope facet enumeration could express the same product under another terminology.
The disjoint-pair case is prior art; originality is restricted to unrestricted cluster cardinalities, overlapping short edges, independent scales and the full classification.
No independent scientific audit has been performed.

value.rationale: Classifies the exact facet invariant for the full natural class of finite independent-scale block-equilateral ultrametrics. The vertex construction is an explicit globally exhaustive structure theorem: unlike the known disjoint-pair case, it permits arbitrarily large clusters with overlapping short edges. For two triples the theorem gives 98 facets, against 62 at the equilateral endpoint, and arbitrary block sizes yield a meaningful multiplicative combinatorial law. This is a motivated polyhedral classification rather than a small instance or mere basis change.
